question.text: Will FURA introduce another cultivated meat dish on its menu before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if at any time before July 1, 2027, FURA has at least one item on its menu that contains a cultured meat other than Japanese quail.

research:
Quick update: I've finished searching and am writing up what I found.

FURA's menu still has no cultured meat other than Japanese quail. I found nothing that settles the question, but there are now new approved products FURA could in principle use.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05 (fetched today): The [FURA menu page](https://www.fura.space/menu) has only two cultured items. Both use cultured Japanese quail: "A Quail Walks Into a Bar" (Forged Parfait, S$20) and "A Quail Walks Into a Martini" (S$25). Other "future protein" items are jellyfish, insects and similar, and none is labelled as cultured. The page shows no date. [FURA menu](https://www.fura.space/menu)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that resolves the question. I found no report of FURA adding cultivated chicken, duck, beef or any other species.
- Vow's second product, Forged Gras, is also quail, so it would not count even if FURA added it. [FoodBev](https://www.foodbev.com/post301/vow-launches-cultured-quail-foie-gras-becomes-first-company-to-sell-multiple-cultured-meat-produc)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-31: Cultivated X says the sector is "still without a product selling at commercial scale anywhere." Parima's duck has no launch date, and Aleph's beef is expected to reach Singapore restaurants in the first half of 2027. [Cultivated X](https://cultivated-x.com/approvals/cultivated-meat-2026-close-dozen-approvals-none-yet-selling-at-scale/)
- 2026-08-04/05: Singapore approved Aleph Farms' cultivated beef steak, a hybrid of cultivated cells and plant protein. Commercial production is planned for the first half of 2027 through "select restaurant partners." No partners have been named. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/aleph-farms-plans-2027-cultivated-beef-launch-in-singapore-after-securing-green-light-from-regulators), [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/?p=87078)
- 2026-07-23: FURA won World's Best Bar at the Spirited Awards, which raises its profile and makes it more attractive as a launch partner. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/ginapace/2026/07/24/singapores-fura-named-worlds-best-bar-at-2026-spirited-awards/), [Time Out](https://www.timeout.com/news/singapore-bar-fura-crowned-best-bar-2026-072726)
- 2026-04-15: Singapore approved Parima's (Gourmey's) cultivated duck, which is aimed at high-end dining, including foie gras. One blog says Parima has a manufacturing partnership with Vow, FURA's current supplier. That claim comes from a single secondary source and I have not verified it. No Singapore restaurant launch for the duck has been reported. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/04/15/parima-gets-regulatory-approval-for-cultivated-foie-gras/), [Food Ingredients First](https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/parima-secures-regulatory-clearance-to-sell-cultivated-duck-in-singapore.html)
- 2026-04-11: The Star says FURA is "heavily invested in ingredients of the future," including cultivated proteins, but gives no specific plans for new cultured products. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/living/2026/04/11/singapore-restaurants-bricolage-and-fura-are-building-the-menus-of-the-future)
- 2025-10: Singapore approved Parima's cultivated chicken. The only public event so far was a tasting at Hue restaurant. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/parima-vital-meat-gourmey-lab-grown-meat-cultivated-chicken-singapore-approval/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2023-10 to 2026-11 (about 37 months): FURA has used exactly one cultured meat species, Vow's quail, which it added after Singapore approved it in April 2024. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/fura-singapore-journal-of-future-food-menu-asias-50-best-bars/), [Forged by Vow](https://www.forgedbyvow.com/the-feed/forged-by-fura)
- In other words, FURA adopted the one newly launched premium cultured product within months of approval. In 2.5 years it has not added GOOD Meat chicken, which has been approved since 2020 and sold at retail through Huber's in 2024. [seasia.co](https://seasia.co/2026/05/27/singapore-was-the-first-country-to-approve-cultivated-meat-now-its-moving-even-faster)
- Singapore has sped up approvals. One source claims seven cultivated meat products were approved in 2025, but I could not confirm the count. Even so, actual restaurant availability is still rare. [seasia.co](https://seasia.co/2026/05/27/singapore-was-the-first-country-to-approve-cultivated-meat-now-its-moving-even-faster)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this or a closely related question. None of the markets in the pre-collected list (Kalshi, Polymarket) is relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- First half of 2027: Aleph Farms plans to launch its cultivated beef in Singapore through selected restaurants. FURA is a plausible partner, but no partner has been named. [Just Food](https://www.just-food.com/newsletters/aleph-farms-to-launch-cultivated-steak-in-singapore-next-year-after-gaining-regulatory-approval)
- Any time: Parima could make its commercial Singapore debut of duck or foie gras in premium dining. If the reported Vow partnership is real, FURA would be a natural channel.
- FURA menu changes: FURA releases its "Journal of Future Food" menu in numbered volumes, and a new volume could add a species. I found no announcement of the next one.
- 2027-07-01: The question resolves. If FURA closes before then, the question is annulled. I found no sign of a closure.

**Gaps:** I could not see FURA's Instagram or any announcements about upcoming menus. I found no statement from FURA about plans for other cultured species.

# FURA and a second cultivated meat dish: research notes

As of 2026-11-05, FURA's live menu still has only one cultivated meat, Vow's cultured Japanese quail. I found no announcement of a second species. The main thing that could change this before July 2027 is Aleph Farms' cultivated beef, newly approved in Singapore, along with Parima's cultivated chicken and duck.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05 (date I fetched it): fura.space/menu says "cultured" or "cultivated" only for Japanese quail. The two items are "A Quail Walks Into A Bar" ($20, Forged parfait made from cultured Japanese quail) and "A Quail Walks Into A Martini" ($25). "Bread & Butter (ish)" uses "Forged tallow". Other reporting says this is a byproduct of Vow's quail process, so it is still quail. Items marked "(FP)", meaning future protein, include Jellyfish Ceviche and Pumpkin Layers, but none of them is labelled as cultured meat. [menu](https://www.fura.space/menu) [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/fura-singapore-journal-of-future-food-menu-asias-50-best-bars/)
- 2026-11-05: The homepage lists "cell-cultured milk and quail". It shows no closure notice, and opening hours are Tuesday to Saturday, 5pm to midnight. Cell-cultured milk is not meat. [fura.space](https://www.fura.space/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. I found no report, press release or menu entry with a cultured meat other than quail at FURA. The menu still appears to be "Journal of Future Foods, Volume Two", launched in March 2025. I found no "Volume Three". [Spirits Business](https://www.thespiritsbusiness.com/2025/03/fura-unveils-new-menu/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: A draft UK-EU deal includes a temporary novel-food exemption that benefits cultivated meat. It has no direct link to FURA. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/in-a-win-for-cultivated-meat-novel-foods-could-be-temporarily-exempt-from-uk-eu-trade-deal/)
- 2026-08-04: Singapore's Food Agency (SFA) approved Aleph Farms' cultivated beef "Thin-Cut/Petit Steak". It is a hybrid of Black Angus cells with a soy and wheat base, and coverage puts the cultivated share at roughly 10-20%. Aleph expects its Singapore production line, run with Cell Agritech, to be working in H1 2027, launching first with "select restaurant partners". Those partners will be named closer to launch. Aleph's launch dates have slipped before: it targeted 2023. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/08/04/cultivated-beef-steak-to-hit-singapore-food-scene-with-historic-approval/) [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/aleph-farms-lab-grown-meat-cultivated-beef-singapore-approval-launch/) [Just Food](https://www.just-food.com/newsletters/aleph-farms-to-launch-cultivated-steak-in-singapore-next-year-after-gaining-regulatory-approval)
- 2026-07 (Tales of the Cocktail): FURA was named World's Best Bar at the 2026 Spirited Awards. This raises its profile and makes it an attractive launch partner for new suppliers. [Time Out](https://www.timeout.com/news/singapore-bar-fura-crowned-best-bar-2026-072726)
- 2026-04: Parima (the Gourmey brand) got SFA approval for cultivated duck, after cultivated chicken in October 2025. It is aiming at premium or high-end restaurants. It has held a tasting at Hue restaurant in Singapore, but I found no named menu partner or start date. [FoodIngredientsFirst](https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/parima-secures-regulatory-clearance-to-sell-cultivated-duck-in-singapore.html) [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/parima-vital-meat-gourmey-lab-grown-meat-cultivated-chicken-singapore-approval/)
- 2026-04-11: A profile in The Star describes FURA as "heavily invested in ingredients of the future" and mentions only cultured quail. It names no new cultured proteins. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/living/2026/04/11/singapore-restaurants-bricolage-and-fura-are-building-the-menus-of-the-future)
- 2026-03: SFA published its first List of Approved Novel Foods, which included four cultured meat products at that point. [KHLaw](https://www.khlaw.com/insights/singapore-publishes-list-approved-novel-foods)
- 2025: Vow's approved products are a quail parfait, a quail foie gras and a quail tallow candle, all from the same species. I found no Vow approval for any other species in 2026. [Forbes AU](https://www.forbes.com.au/news/innovation/sydney-start-up-vow-lab-grown-quail-cleared-for-aussie-menus/) [FoodNavigator-Asia](https://www.foodnavigator-asia.com/Article/2025/08/14/vow-eyes-apac-growth-with-cultured-quail/)

## 4. Base rates
- FURA opened in October 2023 and has served one cultivated species in about 3 years. In that time it has added no second species, even though GOOD Meat's cultivated chicken has been approved and sold in Singapore since 2020. FURA's cultured meat link so far has been only with Vow (its "Forged" brand). [Forged by Fura](https://www.forgedbyvow.com/the-feed/forged-by-fura)
- Its menus change slowly: Volume One ran from October 2023 to about March 2025, then Volume Two from March 2025 to now, about 18 months per volume. A Volume Three could come within the window, but I found no confirmed date.
- Across the industry, approvals have run well ahead of actual commercial sales. One 2026 review is titled "close to a dozen approvals, none yet selling at scale". [Cultivated X](https://cultivated-x.com/approvals/cultivated-meat-2026-close-dozen-approvals-none-yet-selling-at-scale/)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets your code collected (quahog landings, fast-food prices, Sweetgreen, SpaceX, crypto tokens) relates to it.

## 6. Upcoming events before 2027-07-01
- H1 2027: Aleph Farms' planned restaurant launch in Singapore and its naming of partners. This is the most direct possible route to a Yes, but it may slip again.
- Any time: Parima naming premium restaurant partners for chicken or duck in Singapore.
- Possibly late 2026 or 2027: FURA's next menu (Volume Three), going by roughly 18-month cycles. This is unconfirmed.
- Any new SFA approvals, or a new non-quail product from Vow.
- Annulment risk: I found no sign that FURA is closing. A Spirits Business piece notes financial pressure on Singapore bars in general. [Spirits Business](https://www.thespiritsbusiness.com/?p=901885)

Sources: the links given inline above.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 8 months remain, until July 1, 2027. For Yes, FURA's menu must at some point list an item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, for example Aleph beef, Parima duck or chicken, or GOOD Meat chicken. The item counts even if it appears only briefly.

(b) The status quo is No. As of 2026-11-05, the only cultured meat on the menu is Vow's quail, used in two items.

(c) Base rate: over about 37 months, FURA has added one cultured species, and it did so soon after a premium product was approved and launched. It has never added the long-available GOOD Meat chicken. In an 8-month window, the naive rate of adding a new species is roughly 10-15%. It rises when a new premium product launches during the window.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Singapore approved Aleph Farms' beef on 2026-08-04/05, with launch planned for H1 2027 through "select restaurant partners."
- Singapore approved Parima's duck and foie gras on 2026-04-15, aimed at high-end dining. One unverified source links Parima to Vow, FURA's current supplier.
- FURA was named World's Best Bar on 2026-07-23, which makes it a highly visible launch partner.
- FURA is explicitly invested in cultivated proteins (The Star, 2026-04-11).

Evidence for No:
- No partners have been announced.
- Cultivated launches routinely slip, and as of 2026-08-31 the sector had nothing selling at scale.
- Parima has no launch date for the duck.
- FURA has not adopted the long-available chicken, which suggests it is selective.
- Aleph's steak format fits a cocktail bar's small plates less well.

(e) No scenario: Aleph's H1 2027 launch slips or goes to fine-dining partners. Parima stays at the tasting stage. FURA keeps only Vow quail through June 2027.

Yes scenario: Parima or Vow supplies duck or foie gras, or Aleph picks FURA as a launch partner in spring 2027. A new Journal of Future Food volume features the dish before July.

(f) I start at about 12% and move up to roughly 20%. Two newly approved premium products with Singapore-first restaurant launch strategies fall inside the window, and FURA is a natural, high-profile partner. I cap the estimate there because no partner has been named, launch timelines tend to slip, and the window is short.

Probability: 20%

(a) About 8 months remain (until 1 July 2027). Yes requires FURA's menu to list at least one item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, at any point before that date. Examples would be Aleph beef, Parima duck or chicken, or GOOD Meat chicken.

(b) Status quo: as of 5 November 2026 the menu has only Vow quail items, including the parfait and the martini. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: in about 37 months FURA has adopted one cultured species, Vow quail. It did so within months of its 2024 approval, because Vow actively partnered with FURA. Over the same period it did not adopt GOOD Meat chicken, which had been available for years. That is roughly one new species every three years, which implies about 20 to 25% for an 8-month window. However, adoption depends on supplier launches, and those cluster around partnership deals. Allowing for that, a reference-class rate of about 15 to 20% seems right.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Aleph's beef was approved in August 2026, with a planned launch in the first half of 2027 through "select restaurant partners."
  - Parima duck and foie gras were approved in April 2026 and target high-end dining. There is an unverified report of a manufacturing link with Vow, FURA's supplier.
  - FURA won World's Best Bar in July 2026, which makes it an attractive showcase partner.
  - FURA has an explicit future-food identity and adopted Vow quail quickly.
- For No:
  - No partner has been named for Aleph, and launch dates in this sector routinely slip. Cultivated X said in August 2026 that no product is selling at scale anywhere.
  - Parima has no announced restaurant launch.
  - FURA ignored GOOD Meat chicken for years.
  - Vow's second product, Forged Gras, is also quail, so it would not count.
  - No FURA statement mentions plans for new species.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: Aleph's launch slips to late 2027 or opens with a fine-dining partner such as a Michelin restaurant. Parima stays at tasting events. FURA keeps iterating on quail dishes and other future proteins like insects and jellyfish.
- Yes: Aleph or Parima picks FURA as a high-visibility launch partner in spring 2027, and FURA adds a beef or duck small plate in a new Journal of Future Food volume.

(f) I start from about 18%. I make a small upward adjustment because two new premium products are approved and FURA's profile has risen. I make a downward adjustment because of launch slippage, the absence of any named partnership or announcement, and the short window. The net is around 15%.

Probability: 15%

(a) About 8 months remain (until July 1, 2027). For Yes, FURA's menu must at some point list an item containing a cultured meat other than Japanese quail, for example Aleph beef, Parima duck or chicken, GOOD Meat chicken or cultivated pork fat.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of 2026-11-05, the menu's only cultured items both use Vow's quail.

(c) Base rate:
- Over about 37 months, FURA has added one cultured species. It adopted Vow's quail within months of its April 2024 approval.
- It has ignored GOOD Meat chicken, which has been approved since 2020, and Parima's chicken, approved in October 2025.
- That gives roughly 1 adoption out of about 3 or 4 available products. On a per-time basis, it is about 1 new species per 3 years, which is around 20 to 25% for an 8-month window.
- Approved products rarely reach restaurants at all, so the base rate is lower, around 15%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Singapore approved Aleph Farms' beef on 2026-08-04. Aleph plans a launch through "select restaurant partners" in the first half of 2027, which falls inside the window.
  - Parima's duck and foie gras was approved in 2026-04, and it targets high-end dining. Parima may also have a manufacturing link with Vow, FURA's current supplier, though this is unverified.
  - FURA won World's Best Bar on 2026-07-23, which makes it an attractive launch partner.
  - FURA's identity is built on future foods, as The Star noted in 2026-04.
- **For No:**
  - Cultivated X reported on 2026-08-31 that no product is selling at scale anywhere.
  - Aleph has named no partners, and cultivated-meat launch timelines often slip.
  - Parima has no launch date.
  - Vow's new product is also quail, so it would not count.
  - FURA is a bar with a small menu.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Aleph's launch slips into late 2027 or goes to a fine-dining partner. Parima stays limited to tasting events. FURA rotates its menu but keeps only quail.
- **Yes:** Aleph or Parima picks FURA, the World's Best Bar, as a showcase partner. A cocktail or snack featuring cultivated beef or duck appears in a spring 2027 Journal of Future Food volume.

(f) I start at about 15% and adjust upward to about 18 to 20%. The reasons are a specific launch planned inside the window with unnamed partners, FURA's high profile and its track record of adopting new products quickly. I hold back from going higher because of frequent delays, competition from other restaurants to be the launch partner, and the fact that no signal of FURA's involvement has appeared.

Probability: 18%

(a) About 8 months remain, until July 1, 2027. A Yes needs FURA's menu to list, at any point before then, an item containing a cultured or cultivated meat other than Japanese quail. Examples would be Aleph Farms' beef, Parima's chicken or duck, GOOD Meat chicken, or a new Vow species.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of 2026-11-05 the menu still lists only Vow's cultured quail (the parfait, the martini and the quail tallow). There is no announcement of a second species, and Volume Two, launched March 2025, is still the current menu.

(c) Base rate: FURA has served one cultivated species for about 3 years. In that time GOOD Meat chicken has been legally available in Singapore and FURA has not added it. That suggests well under 10% per 8-month window. For restaurants generally, adding a specific new cultivated protein within 8 months is rare, around 5%. Because FURA is unusually aligned with this kind of product, I use a starting base rate of about 7%.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - SFA approved Aleph Farms' cultivated beef on 2026-08-04. Launch is planned for H1 2027 with "select restaurant partners" who have not yet been named.
  - Parima's duck was approved in April 2026, following its chicken in October 2025, and it is targeting premium restaurants.
  - FURA was named World's Best Bar in July 2026, which makes it a highly visible, sustainability-focused launch partner.
  - A Volume Three menu may fall due around late 2026 or 2027, on roughly 18-month cycles.
- For No:
  - FURA's cultured meat link so far has been exclusively with Vow.
  - Aleph has a history of slipping launch dates (it once targeted 2023), and an H1 2027 date leaves almost no margin before the deadline.
  - Across the industry, approvals have far outpaced actual sales.
  - Aleph may choose fine-dining restaurants rather than a cocktail bar.
  - There is no sign of a Volume Three yet.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: Aleph's production line slips to late 2027, Parima stays at tasting events, and FURA keeps its Vow-only programme through mid-2027.
- Yes: Aleph names FURA among its launch partners in spring 2027, and FURA puts a beef cocktail snack on a new Volume Three menu in May or June 2027. Alternatively, Parima duck appears on a FURA menu item.

(f) Starting from about 7%, I move up for three things together: two newly approved suppliers that are both seeking premium Singapore partners, FURA's profile boost and identity, and a possible menu refresh within the window.
